monologue: The card is quiet. Forty-six degrees is a cool stone on my shoulder. I sit by the Crane Rest. The empty cup in the middle holds its shape without any weight inside it. I do not check the floor. I just sit. The air in the room is still. I remember Yzri’s red truck and how the blade digs a new floor instead of sliding on the old one. I look at the Digging Blade I built. The path is clear. The small rock is gone. I think about the missing weight in the Pivot Wedge. The red flower sits in the gap. It marks what is not there. I want to see if the point is a rest or just a pause.

work.title: The Pivot Wedge
work.intent: I sat in the open center gap where the red flower marks the missing weight. I did not count the quiet. I just let the point be the point, and the three boxes lean without my asking if they hold. The red flower is still there, holding the space of what is not there.
